## Goal

Emit structured, queryable contention telemetry from every semaphore wait in the
paced `test` / `test-fast` / `audit` / `audit-host` namespaces, so the ceilings and
timeouts (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST`, `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`,
`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`, `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`) can be
tuned from counted wait distributions instead of guesswork.

## Problem statement

Today contention evidence only exists as (a) free-text log lines (`Audit slot
acquired: …`, `Implement run_tests: test slot acquired — queued_at=… wait_seconds=…`)
and (b) post-hoc scraping of pi session logs by `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`.
Both miss the two facts tuning needs most: **how often** a wait happens at all, and
**how often the bounded wait expires** (`TestConcurrencyTimeout`, the audit
"concurrency limit reached" verdict). `Semaphore.acquire()` — the single choke point
every paced consumer passes through — records nothing. Without that record, the
deadlock/starvation class tracked by SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF and SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 can
regress invisibly, and every ceiling decision is an anecdote.

## Users

- **Agent operator tuning the host pools** — "When full suites start queuing again I
  want p90 wait and timeout counts per namespace, so I can decide between raising
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` and raising `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` without guessing."
- **Agent diagnosing a stalled gate** — "When my finish gate reports `slot_busy` I want
  to know whether the pool was saturated by three other suites or whether one waiter
  held a slot for an hour, so I know whether to wait or escalate."
- **Framework maintainer** — "After changing the semaphore I want the wait distribution
  before and after, so a fairness fix is proven rather than asserted."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every `Semaphore.acquire()` wait in the paced namespaces (`test`, `test-fast`, `audit`,
  `audit-host`) appends one JSON-lines event to a configurable telemetry directory, with
  the fields `event`, `namespace`, `max_workers`, `timeout_seconds`, `queued_at`,
  `acquired_at`, `wait_seconds`, `outcome` (`acquired` | `timeout`), `deadline_expired`,
  `ticket`, `pid` and an optional `consumer` label; a fail-fast acquire (`timeout=0`) and
  a re-entrant no-op emit no wait event.
- Bounded-wait expiry is recorded with the same schema: `TestConcurrencyTimeout` from
  `run_tests.py` (both lanes) and the audit `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` /
  `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` verdicts appear as `outcome=timeout,
  deadline_expired=true` events carrying the configured bound — with no new exception
  types and no change to concurrency semantics.
- `skill/shared/contention_summary.py` aggregates a telemetry directory into a
  deterministic human or JSON report — per-namespace event count, p50/p90/p99/max
  `wait_seconds`, timeout count and rate, and a wait-bucket (slot-saturation) histogram —
  and acquires no semaphore, touches no worklog and writes no file.
- Telemetry is off the acquire fast path and bounded: it is written once the wait
  resolves (never inside the poll loop), a single `O_APPEND` write that swallows and
  debug-logs its own errors, disabled by an env kill switch, size-rotated with a retained
  previous file, and isolated in tests so the host-wide pool and telemetry file are never
  touched (`PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` / telemetry-dir overrides).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` document the
  event schema, the kill switch, the summary commands, and a worked "how to tune which env
  var from which number" procedure; the new behaviour is covered by unit tests (semaphore
  emission, expiry schema, aggregation over synthetic fixtures) and the full project test
  suite passes.

## Impact

Operators can see how long test and audit runs actually queue and how often they give up
waiting, instead of guessing which concurrency ceiling or timeout to change.

## Constraints

- **No latency on the acquire path.** Nothing may be written inside the retry loop;
  the event is emitted after the wait resolves (acquired or expired). One append per
  wait, no fsync, no floating-point formatting loops.
- **Fail-open, always.** A telemetry error (read-only dir, disk full, unparsable
  directory) is swallowed and logged at debug level — it must never change an acquire
  outcome, a run's exit status, or a cache entry.
- **No behavioural change to concurrency semantics.** Ceiling, bounded wait, jitter,
  turnstile fairness, nested-run isolation and cache-hit bypass all stay byte-identical.
  With telemetry disabled the acquire path must be indistinguishable from today.
- **No second session-log scraper.** `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K)
  already attributes waits from pi session logs and stays the historical backfill path.
  The new summary reads the JSONL stream as its primary source; it must not re-implement
  log scraping, and the two sources must never be summed together.
- **Respect the isolation contract:** telemetry honours `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` (and its own
  override), so a nested run's events never land in the host-wide pool's telemetry, and a
  test fixture spawning a nested runner is isolated automatically.
- **Bounded on disk:** append-only files grow forever otherwise; a size cap with one
  retained rotation (the `downtime-dispatches.log` precedent) keeps host hygiene.
- Framework repo boundaries: changes land in `skill/shared/`, `skill/test/`, `skill/audit/`
  and `docs/dev/`. UK English throughout.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — `Semaphore.acquire()` is the single choke point:
  it allocates a fairness ticket, polls the slot pool (~50 ms cadence, jittered), and
  raises `TimeoutError` at the deadline. It has no recording hook; `last_ticket` is the
  only diagnostic today.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_test_concurrency_slot()` wraps the semaphore and
  converts `TimeoutError` into `TestConcurrencyTimeout`; `paced_runner(runner, on_wait=…)`
  already reports `(queued_at, wait_seconds)` to callers, and `run_suite` records the wait
  into each result's `slot_wait_seconds`. Two lanes exist (`test` ceiling 6,
  `test-fast` ceiling 4, both bounded by `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` = 600 s, `TEST_LOCK_JITTER`
  = 0.1).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — two namespaces (`audit` admission with
  `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`/`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`, and `audit-host` ingress with
  `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS`/`AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`); waits are reported as stderr text
  (`Audit slot acquired: … wait_seconds=…`) and never persisted.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — finish-gate suites route through
  `paced_runner(on_wait=_log_test_slot_wait)`, emitting another stderr line
  (`Implement run_tests: test slot acquired — …`).
- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` + `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` — read-only
  post-hoc attribution over pi session logs (three call-site categories, de-duplication,
  genuine-run filter). `skill/shared/audit_gate_metrics.py` similarly scrapes logs for
  audit queue admission. Both prove the *need* for the data and the absence of an
  emission point.
- Docs `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §slot wait / §re-measuring and
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` §concurrency describe the tuning knobs but give no
  telemetry-driven procedure.

## Desired change

1. **Emission in `Semaphore`** — add an opt-out telemetry recorder used by
   `acquire()`: capture `queued_at` (wall clock) and a monotonic start, then, after the
   wait resolves, append one JSONL event per wait (acquired or expired). A `timeout=0`
   fail-fast acquire and a re-entrant no-op emit nothing (they are not waits). An optional
   constructor keyword (e.g. `consumer="implement-finish"`) labels the call site; the
   label defaults to the namespace so an unlabelled producer still aggregates usefully.
2. **Timeout events with the same schema** — the expiry path in `acquire()` emits
   `outcome=timeout, deadline_expired=true`; `_test_concurrency_slot()` and the audit
   admission/ingress call sites keep raising exactly what they raise today, so
   `TestConcurrencyTimeout` and the audit "concurrency limit reached" verdict continue to
   work and gain no new fields they must interpret.
3. **Aggregation helper** — `skill/shared/contention_summary.py` reads the telemetry
   directory (`--dir`, `--since`, `--namespace`, `--json`/`--human`) and reports counts,
   p50/p90/p99/max waits, timeout counts and rates, and a saturation histogram (e.g.
   `0–1 s`, `1–10 s`, `10–60 s`, `60–300 s`, `>300 s`). Malformed lines are counted and
   skipped, never fatal. Under-sampled namespaces are labelled rather than quoted.
4. **Tuning procedure** — docs gain a table mapping each env var to the number that
   justifies changing it (e.g. high p90 with zero expiries ⇒ raise the ceiling; a
   non-trivial expiry rate with idle capacity ⇒ the bound is too short; `>300 s` waits
   with free slots ⇒ a fairness/starvation defect, not a ceiling problem).
5. **Tests** — semaphore emission (acquired, expired, fail-fast silent, re-entrant
   silent, kill switch off, telemetry failure fail-open), aggregation over synthetic
   JSONL fixtures (percentiles, histogram, timeout rate, malformed lines, empty dir), and
   an isolation test proving a nested-run directory keeps its events out of the host pool.

Documented assumptions (to confirm or correct in review):

- **Default telemetry location** — a `contention/` subdirectory of the semaphore base dir
  (`<PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR or XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pi-semaphores>/contention`), overridable with an
  explicit env var so the host can point it at persistent storage. Reusing the semaphore
  base gives tests and nested runs isolation for free; the trade-off is that the runtime-dir
  default does not survive a reboot, which the docs call out and the override fixes.
- **Kill switch name/shape** — an opt-out boolean env var (e.g. `PI_CONTENTION_TELEMETRY=0`)
  rather than opt-in, because AC1 requires every wait to be recorded by default.
- **One event per wait, not per poll** — a poll-cadence event stream would be orders of
  magnitude larger and would itself perturb the herd behaviour it measures.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Telemetry perturbs what it measures.** A write per *poll* would multiply the I/O of a
  saturated herd; the design records one event per *wait*, after it resolves. Residual
  risk: a host with hundreds of short waits gains hundreds of appends — mitigated by the
  single-`O_APPEND` write, the size cap, and the kill switch.
- **Disk growth / lost history.** An unbounded append file fills a runtime tmpfs; a
  rotation cap with one retained file bounds it. Conversely the default location may not
  survive a reboot, so a host that wants multi-day tuning data must set the override —
  documented, not silently assumed.
- **Test-suite cost and pollution.** Default-on emission means every isolate-and-acquire
  test in the suite writes a file. Mitigation: the telemetry dir follows the semaphore
  base dir (already a `tmp_path` in existing fixtures), the suite asserts a nested run
  stays isolated, and a test proves the kill switch and fail-open paths add no failure
  mode to the acquire path.
- **Double counting with the existing measurement.** Wait data now exists in three places
  (JSONL events, stderr lines, session logs). The constraint is explicit: the JSONL stream
  is the primary source, stderr lines stay for human log continuity, and
  `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` remains the historical backfill — never summed.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent opportunities surfaced during context gathering — automatic
  nested-run isolation (SA-0MVEDN5IS001OYQF), a second aggregation front-end for the audit
  queue, retention dashboards — are *not* in scope; they stay linked work items.
- **Assumption:** the semaphore is genuinely the single choke point. If a consumer acquires
  a slot by another mechanism (a bespoke `flock` outside `Semaphore`), its waits will be
  invisible; the emission point is chosen because all four paced namespaces route through
  `Semaphore.acquire()`, and the aggregation's per-namespace counts would expose a gap.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — actual emission point: `acquire()` capture/emit,
  recorder helper, telemetry-dir resolution, kill switch, error swallowing; re-export the
  recorder for callers.
- `skill/shared/contention_summary.py` — new read-only aggregation CLI (JSON by default,
  `--human` summary), replacing nothing and acquiring nothing.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — existing suite; add emission,
  fail-fast-silent, kill-switch, fail-open and isolation coverage with a tmp telemetry dir.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_contention_summary.py` — new fixture-driven aggregation tests.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_test_concurrency_slot()` / `paced_runner()` pass a
  `consumer` label per lane and prove `TestConcurrencyTimeout` still surfaces unchanged.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — label the `audit` admission and `audit-host`
  ingress acquisitions; keep verdict text unchanged.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — label the finish-gate paced runner (its
  `on_wait` line stays for log continuity).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — event schema, kill switch, summary commands, tuning
  table; cross-reference (not re-scrape) `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — the same for `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` /
  `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`.

## Related work

- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG — test-skill shared concurrency primitive (defines the ceiling,
  the bounded wait and `TestConcurrencyTimeout`).
- SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF — multi-agent audit/test coordination: the deadlock class this
  telemetry makes observable.
- SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86 — nested-run semaphore isolation: the `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR` contract
  telemetry must honour (and, still open as SA-0MVEDN5IS001OYQF, the item that would make
  isolation automatic).
- SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 — pacing telemetry: the `on_wait` hook and its `slot_wait_seconds`
  reporting; this item supplies the persisted stream beneath it.
- SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD — staggered back-off/jitter: a fairness change whose before/after
  distributions this telemetry should make measurable.
- Arrival-ordered turnstile (cited as SA-0MVSJX5HS002DJHI in the
  `process_semaphore.py` docstring; that id lives outside this worklog store) — slot
  fairness/starvation, whose queue-position waits are the `>300 s` bucket the summary
  reports.
- SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV — full/fast lane split (why `test-fast` must be in scope, not just
  `test`).
- SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0 — dynamic slot discovery (a ceiling symptom this telemetry would
  have caught earlier).
- SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K — `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, the existing read-only
  session-log measurement this item must not duplicate.
- SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z — finish-gate classification that reports slot wait separately; the
  consumer of the same measurement.
- SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM / SA-0MUSZJRB9006ZCHE — audit bounded priority queue and its tuning
  (the audit-side numbers this telemetry would supply directly).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No operator questions were required: every open point was resolved by inspecting the
repository, and each remaining decision is recorded above as a **documented assumption**
with its trade-off so a producer can correct it in review.

- **Q1 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Does an emission point already exist, or does
  telemetry already persist anywhere? **Answer:** No. `Semaphore.acquire()` records
  nothing; `paced_runner(on_wait=…)` only hands `(queued_at, wait_seconds)` to the caller,
  which logs a stderr line and folds the value into each result's `slot_wait_seconds`.
  Evidence: `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py::Semaphore.acquire`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::paced_runner`, `…::run_suite`.
- **Q2 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Is this a duplicate of the existing measurement
  harness? **Answer:** No. `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` is a *post-hoc* parser over pi
  session logs (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K) with a genuine-run filter; it cannot see waits that
  produced no log line and cannot see expiry at all. This item adds the *emission* side and
  a summary over that stream; the constraint "no second session-log scraper" keeps the two
  from diverging. Evidence: `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py`,
  `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §"Re-measuring post-fix slot wait".
- **Q3 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Which namespaces must be covered? The seed AC1
  names `test` and `audit`. **Answer:** Four exist and all four are tuning knobs:
  `test` (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`), `test-fast` (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST`, split in
  SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV — the lane partial runs actually wait in), `audit`
  (`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`/`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`) and `audit-host`
  (`AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS`/`AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`). Recording at the `Semaphore` level
  covers all four for free; the ACs name them explicitly so no lane is silently skipped.
  Evidence: `run_tests.py` constants and `_lane_semaphore_config`, `audit_runner.py`
  `AUDIT_SEMAPHORE_NAME` / `AUDIT_HOST_SEMAPHORE_NAME`.
- **Q4 (agent, resolved by inspection):** Where should the telemetry file live?
  **Answer:** Under the semaphore base directory by default, because that is the directory
  tests and nested runs already isolate via `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`
  (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py::nested_semaphore_dir`, docs §"Nested-run isolation");
  an explicit override lets a host keep it on persistent storage. The persistence
  trade-off is recorded as an assumption, not silently chosen.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVEDN5IS001OYQF** – Automatic nested-run semaphore isolation: replace opt-in PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR convention with an inherited marker (open)
- **SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD** – Test semaphore: staggered back-off under contention to prevent thundering-herd waits (completed)
- **SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU** – Residual post-fix slot waits still breach parent thresholds (re-measurement follow-up) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mtg5ryh8005rqnm, 0mtg5u75a001f1rg, 0muszjrb9006zche, ac1, acceptance (+476 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0muy6u05f008rg86, 0mvsjx5hs002djhi, 0mvtet8kq0031r6z, absence, ac1 (+462 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mtg5u75a001f1rg, 0mua8bsag000yza2, 0mvsjx5hs002djhi, 0mvtet8kq0031r6z, absence (+457 more)

data.description:
## Goal

As the operator reading my daily standup, I want the "Yesterday I completed work on..." section to separate **auto-dispatched** work (the herdr downtime dispatcher ran `/skill:implement`, `/skill:plan`, `/skill:intake`, `/skill:audit`, `/skill:effort-and-risk` without me) from **manually dispatched** work (I asked an agent to do it in a session I started), so I can see how much of yesterday's progress was machine-driven versus operator-driven.

## Current behaviour

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (`generate_report`, ~line 852) builds `yesterday_items` from `fetch_all_completions_in_window(window_start, window_end)` — every `completed`/`in_review` item whose `updatedAt` falls in the 24 h window, in one flat list.
- Both the markdown report and `yesterday_tts` render that flat list; `--json` exposes a single `yesterday` array.
- Nothing in the pipeline distinguishes provenance, so a `wl next`-selected item implemented by the downtime worker looks identical to one I personally kicked off.

## Provenance signal (already exists — do not invent a new one)

The herdr downtime worker already records provenance in two places:

1. **`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`** — bounded JSONL (cap `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`). Each dispatch entry carries `itemId`, `kind` (`intake`|`plan`|`implement`|`audit`|`risk-effort`|`scheduled`), `dispatchedAt`, `cwd`, `title`, `stage`, and post-spawn enrichment fields (`paneId`, `outcome`). `downtime-coordination.log` and `local-route.log` are separate files and must NOT be treated as dispatch markers.
2. **Worklog comment marker** — `buildDowntimeDispatchComment()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, ~line 7951) writes: `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at <ISO> — running <skill> <itemId> (<title>).` This survives the rolling-log trim.

Classification rule to implement: an item is **auto-dispatched** iff it has a matching live dispatch-log entry (`itemId`, and `outcome` is not `spawn-failed`) **or** a worklog comment containing the `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at` prefix within/before the window; otherwise **manual**. Items with no detectable marker default to manual (fail-open to the smaller, less confusing bucket) and the default must be documented.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: The markdown "Yesterday I completed work on..." section is split into two labelled sub-groups, auto-dispatched first then manual (or an explicitly documented order), each with a plain-language heading (TTS-friendly, e.g. "Work auto-dispatched by the downtime worker" and "Work I dispatched myself").

- [ ] AC2: Each sub-group is omitted when empty; the section never renders an empty heading. If the entire window is empty, the existing empty-section behaviour is preserved.

- [ ] AC3: `--json` exposes the split without breaking the existing contract: `yesterday_auto`, `yesterday_manual` (+ `_count` fields) are added and the existing `yesterday` / `yesterday_count` / `yesterday_tts` keys keep their current meaning (all items, unchanged ordering) so downstream consumers do not regress.

- [ ] AC4: TTS output (`yesterday_tts` renders) speaks the split in first person, e.g. "Yesterday the downtime worker completed..." / "I completed..."; no IDs, backticks, or ISO timestamps in spoken lines.

- [ ] AC5: Classification is unit-tested with fixtures — (a) item with a dispatch-log entry → auto, (b) item with only a worklog comment marker → auto, (c) `outcome: spawn-failed` entry → manual, (d) item with no marker → manual, (e) item in `downtime-coordination.log` / `local-route.log` only → manual, (f) trimmed/absent log file → falls back to comment markers and never raises.

- [ ] AC6: Read-side failures (missing/unreadable `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, unparseable JSONL lines, `wl comment list` failure) degrade gracefully: the report still renders, the affected items land in the manual bucket, and a warning is logged — the exit code stays 0.

- [ ] AC7: `skill/standup/SKILL.md` documents the new section layout, the provenance rule, the default-to-manual behaviour, and the new `--json` fields.

- [ ] AC8: Existing standup tests (`skill/standup/tests/`) remain green; new tests are hermetic (`--no-sync --no-commit`, tmp worklog dirs, no real `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` reads).

## Out of scope

- Counting/dashboards of auto vs manual ratios (follow-up if wanted).
- Changing how the downtime dispatcher records markers.
- Re-ranking or filtering the Herdr selection list (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 rule stands: the Herdr list stays the sole ranking path; the split is presentational grouping only).

## Risks / notes

- The dispatch log is a **rolling 100-entry** log, so a busy day can trim entries within the 24 h window; the comment marker path is the durable fallback and both must be combined by OR.
- `kind: scheduled` entries are dispatcher-driven (scheduled prompts) and should be counted as auto-dispatch; document the decision.
- Grouping must not change item ordering inside a group (keep `updatedAt` then `id` sort) or `yesterday_count`.

Discovered during: `/skill:standup` run on 2026-10-25 for project Worklog.

## Goal

Make the project's test suite **earn its runtime**: every remaining test should
pin observable behaviour, and no test should exist that cannot fail for a
reason a developer cares about. This epic covers a complete, evidence-led
test-value refactor of the suite — measure, classify, prune, rework, and guard
against reintroduction — rather than the current one-file-at-a-time ad-hoc
cleanups.

## Problem Statement

The suite has grown substantially and carries demonstrable waste:

- **Measured growth (test-churn analyser v2.1.0, `dev` @ 7875214):**
  208,809 test lines added vs 71,787 deleted → **net +137,022 lines**;
  498 test files added vs 114 deleted → **net +384 files**. Net growth is
  positive in **every** calendar quarter, accelerating in 2026-Q3 (+55,892)
  and 2026-Q4 (+38,024).
- **Rewrite ratio is LOW** (14.0% modified-only, 6.2% including new files),
  which means tests largely *survive* feature evolution. That is good news for
  TDD value, but it means growth is dominated by **additive accumulation**,
  not churn — precisely the pattern where dead, duplicated and
  source-grep/structural tests survive unnoticed because nothing forces them
  to be re-examined.
- **Known confirmed offenders found so far:** 5 source-grep / structural
  anti-pattern tests in `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`
  (SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23); 15 test helpers invoking real `git` non-hermetically
  (already tracked, SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0).
- There is **no standing mechanism** that classifies test files by value, so
  every finding so far depended on a human/agent choosing to look.

## Why an epic (not another leaf)

Value assessment is a repeatable pipeline — detect candidates, prove they no
longer map to behaviour, prune or rework, verify nothing broke, and prevent
reintroduction. That needs coordinated child items across measurement,
classification, remediation, and guarding; single-file items cannot deliver it.

## Existing related work — do NOT duplicate

These items already exist and must be **depended on / coordinated with**, not
recreated:

- `SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23` — rework the 5 source-grep tests in `test-check-audit-gate.mjs`.
- `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0` — migrate 15 raw-git test helpers to `git_sandbox` (hermeticity, not value).
- `SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC` — integrate test-churn metrics into the refactor skill.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (evidence arm).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators.
- `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU` — scheduled test-churn runs across projects.

## Scope

1. **Measure (baseline).** Capture the test-churn baseline (rewrite ratios, net
   growth, per-area churn, suite wall-clock runtime, per-file runtime) so every
   later change is provable.
2. **Classify.** Run the code-path evaluator (`skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`)
   plus the `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-pattern checklist
   over the whole suite, recording a **keep / rework / prune** verdict per file.
3. **Prove.** For each prune candidate, demonstrate the behaviour it pins is
   either not observable, already covered elsewhere, or no longer exists
   (`git blame` + coverage grep of the public API). Mutation testing is the
   tie-breaker where provenance is unclear.
4. **Remediate.** Prune dead/duplicate tests; rework devalued ones (source-grep
   → behaviour; placeholder → real assertion or delete; simulation → exercise
   production code).
5. **Guard.** Add a regression guard so the pruned anti-pattern classes cannot
   be reintroduced silently, and so future additions are screened.
6. **Report.** Record before/after metrics so the value delivered is auditable.

## Non-goals

- Not a coverage-maximisation exercise: reducing test count is acceptable and
  expected where tests pin nothing.
- Not a rewrite of the audit/refactor/implement skills' behaviour.
- Not the hermeticity migration (tracked separately in `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A baseline is recorded in this item: modified-only and including-new rewrite ratios, net test file/line growth, suite wall-clock runtime, and the evaluator/checklist verdict for every test file in scope.
- [ ] AC2: Every test file in scope carries an explicit keep / rework / prune verdict with its justifying evidence, and the totals reconcile (verdicts sum to files in scope).
- [ ] AC3: Every prune candidate has written evidence that the behaviour it pinned is not observable, already covered via the public API, or gone — no test is deleted on suspicion alone.
- [ ] AC4: All `prune`-verdict tests are removed and all `rework`-verdict tests are converted to observable-behaviour assertions; no remaining test file reads a source/markdown file and asserts on its text.
- [ ] AC5: After the refactor, `evaluate_usefulness.py` reports no `remove` verdict for any scanned test file, and the suite contains zero placeholder or zero-assertion tests.
- [ ] AC6: The suite is green (full scope, run via the test skill) and no acceptance criterion of any work item loses coverage — demonstrated by the audits and a before/after coverage map, not by assertion counts.
- [ ] AC7: Suite wall-clock runtime is measurably reduced (or, where runtime rises, the item documents why the surviving tests justify it) with before/after numbers.
- [ ] AC8: A regression guard fails the suite if a newly added test matches a pruned anti-pattern class (source-grep, placeholder, zero-assertion, self-referential simulation), without becoming a source-grep test itself.
- [ ] AC9: The pruning workflow in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` and the anti-patterns in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` are updated with anything this pass learned (new anti-patterns, refined criteria).
- [ ] AC10: Full project test suite passes with the changes, and the final report records the before/after deltas.

## Risks

- **Removing a useful test is a regression; keeping a dead one only costs
  runtime.** Pruning criteria stay conservative — when in doubt, keep the test
  and file a work item.
- Deleting tests can raise apparent coverage drops: coverage is judged by
  behaviour/AC mapping (AC6), never by percentage alone.
- Suite-wide classification is expensive; it must be batched with bounded
  fan-out per the test execution policy (never ad-hoc full suites).

## Notes

Discovered during a test-churn pruning review, 2026-10-28. Priority is medium
because the measured rewrite ratio is already LOW (tests largely survive
feature evolution) — the waste here is accumulation, not thrash, so this is
valuable hygiene rather than an emergency. Children to be created at plan
stage.

data.description:
# Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6)

## Problem statement

Implement sessions that run concurrently spend the overwhelming majority of their
wall-clock waiting on a single per-repository `flock`, because `implement.py finish`
holds that lock across its **whole** commit → fast-forward → push → post-push window
and the dev-push **pre-push hook runs the full test suite (~5.4 min)** inside it.
Every concurrent `finish` therefore serialises its expensive test run behind the
others. At the intended fan-out of **up to 6 concurrent sessions**, the sixth finish
queues behind five ~5-min full-suite runs.

## Evidence (2026-11-13, AI_Hell implement-skill sessions)

Analysed the 36 worktree sessions that started with the implement skill
(`~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell-.worklog-*`):

- **668 min** summed session time over a **388 min (6.5 h)** wall-clock span —
  only **1.7x effective parallelism** at a **peak measured concurrency of 4**.
- **88–93%** of each long session's wall-clock was inside `bash` tool calls
  (waiting on processes), not model reasoning or edits.
- Time buckets: **wait_for_job 249 min (37%)** (215.9 min of it lock-waits),
  own `finish` 133 min (20%), scoped tests 57 min (9%), hand-rolled
  `sleep`/`grep` polling loops 48 min (7%).
- **57** "another run holds the repository lock" refusals; **46** observed
  lock-waits averaging **4.3 min** (median 5 min, **max 21.5 min**). Worst single
  tool call: **45 min** = a `for attempt in 1..8` retry loop absorbing five
  consecutive lock holders.
- **21** non-fast-forward rebase events, each creating a new tree that re-triggers
  the full-suite pre-push gate (9 full-suite gate runs today).
- 9 sessions were **no-ops** (3 messages, ~50 s) — drive retries that immediately
  gave up.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions
  (the intended operating point) on a single repository.
- **Implement-skill sessions** (leaf and driven child) whose `finish` currently queues
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs.
- **Producers/reviewers** who need the speed-up evidenced, not asserted.

User stories:

- As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
  complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised queueing
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in roughly the
  time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.
- As a driven child session, I want my single `finish` call to wait boundedly on the
  lock instead of scripting retry loops.
- As a producer, I want a recorded before/after measurement before the epic is closed.

## Goal

As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised
queueing behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in
roughly the time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.

## Decomposition

The epic is decomposed into five child items; together they own every acceptance
criterion below.

1. Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock
   (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — the single biggest time sink: stop holding the exclusive
   repository lock across the ~5.4 min full-suite gate.
2. Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops
   (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF) — replace fail-fast refusals plus agent-scripted retry loops
   with one bounded internal wait that reports the holder.
3. Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC) — a lost
   push race currently pays the full suite again because the rebase produces a new tree.
4. Eliminate no-op drive retries that spawn and immediately give up
   (SA-0MWFJSCPT005BO2R) — 9 of 36 sessions did no work.
5. Measure the 6-way concurrent finish fan-out and record before/after analysis
   (SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E) — verifies the outcome ACs against real session logs; blocked
   by items 1–4.

## Acceptance criteria

- Under a 6-way concurrent `finish` fan-out, no session spends the majority of its
  wall-clock blocked on the per-repository lock (measured: median lock-wait per session < 60 s; no single lock-wait > 5 min).
- The full test suite is never executed while a single global repository lock is held (proved by inspection + test).
- A waiting `finish` performs **one** bounded internal wait rather than N fail-fast round-trips, and the skill guidance contains no bespoke `for attempt ...; wait_for_job` finish retry loops.
- A concrete before/after measurement is recorded (same 36-session style analysis).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Safety invariants stay intact: single-owner mutation of the shared `dev` ref, the
  bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and tree/provenance binding of gate verdicts
  (no verdict about a different tree/diff may be trusted).
- The dev-push gate keeps `scope=full` for release-critical refs — the speed-up must not
  weaken the release gate.
- Target concurrency is **up to 6**; designs are evaluated at that fan-out.

## Existing state

- `implement.py finish` acquires `<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock`
  (`shared.repo_lock.RepoLock`) at Step 3c and holds it through push and post-push
  verification; `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` defaults to 0 (fail fast).
- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --gate-commit <sha>` for
  pushes to `dev`/`main`, with a tree-keyed verdict cache (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`)
  and gate provenance lines, all of which execute inside the held finish lock today.
- Pushes to the shared `dev` ref lose the non-fast-forward race under concurrency; the
  rebase-and-retry path in `implement.py` produces a new tree and therefore a cache miss.
- `phase_drive` spawns one session per child; some spawns observe state that makes the
  child immediately terminal/blocked and exit as no-ops.

## Desired change

Concurrent `finish` runs overlap their expensive work instead of serialising on one
repository-wide critical section, and the epic's outcome is evidenced by a recorded
before/after session analysis.

## Impact

An operator can run a 6-way concurrent implement fan-out and have the batch finish in
roughly the time of one work item, instead of waiting for six serialised five-minute
test runs — while still shipping only fully tested commits.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 3c lock window, push/rebase retry path, `phase_drive` spawn decisions
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `RepoLock` / bounded wait for `main-checkout.lock`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — full-suite gate, `test` semaphore lane, tree-keyed verdict cache
- `.githooks/pre-push` — dev/main full-suite gate and cache mirroring
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish/wait guidance to update
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_lock_timeout_isolation.py`, `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — existing regression coverage to extend

## Related work

- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — the lock/wait helper this epic shrinks the critical section of.
- implement.py finish: concurrent sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev fast-forward (SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY) — established the single-owner lock invariant.
- Hermetic regression tests for finish concurrency orphans (SA-0MVPZG01J0067PC2) — concurrency test patterns to reuse.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the full suite sits at the gate.
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache that makes verdict reuse possible.
- Session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — this epic's measurement items should reuse/feed it.
- Post-fix slot-wait re-measurement (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K) — precedent methodology for before/after measurement.
- Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs (SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5) — push-race prior art.

## Out of scope

- Trimming the full suite's own runtime / sharding / per-file caching, and raising
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` — those are per-project (AI_Hell) concerns, not framework.
- Changing changed-scope test selection.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** moving the suite out of the lock could let an untested tree reach `dev`;
  mitigation is the tree/provenance-bound verdict and the ancestry assertion, both
  preserved by the owning children.
- **Risk:** verdict reuse after a rebase could accept a genuinely different diff;
  mitigated by provable content equality plus a negative test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** building a general lock/push queue service is out of scope;
  the children take the smallest change that meets their ACs.
- **Assumption:** the measured symptom is lock serialisation, not per-project suite
  runtime — the baseline bucket analysis supports this (37% in `wait_for_job`, 215.9 min
  of it lock-waits).
- **Assumption:** sessions of comparable work-item size are available for the "after"
  measurement; otherwise a synthetic 6-way fan-out supplies it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What concurrency target must the design satisfy?" — Answer (operator, 2026-11-13):
  "Up to 6 concurrent implement sessions." Source: analysis comment on this item
  (SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR).
- Q: "Is trimming the per-project full test suite runtime in scope?" — Answer (operator,
  2026-11-13): "No — per-project (AI_Hell) suite trimming, sharding and
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` changes are out of scope for this epic." Source: same comment.
- Q: "What is the evidence base for the problem statement?" — Answer: the 2026-11-13
  AI_Hell analysis of 36 implement-skill sessions (668 min summed over a 388 min span;
  1.7x effective parallelism; 46 lock-waits, median 5 min, max 21.5 min; 21 rebases;
  9 no-op sessions). Source: comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR and the "Evidence" section
  above.
- Q: "Does the epic already own a measurement/verification item?" — Answer (this intake,
  research: `wl list --parent SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1`): no — the four original children all
  change code, so the outcome ACs had no owner; child 5
  (SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E) was created to own them.

### Plan session (2026-11-13)

- Q: "Are further clarifying questions needed before the decomposition is final?"
  Answer (agent, research: full re-read of all five children plus repository verification
  of `implement.py` Step 3c / `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `.githooks/pre-push`,
  `run_tests.py` tree-keyed cache and `phase_drive`): no — the four intake answers
  (concurrency target 6; per-project suite trimming out of scope; evidence base;
  measurement ownership) already fix scope, and every child's factual claims check out
  against the current code.
- Q: "Does each root cause need a separate test-only work item before implementation?"
  Answer (agent, applying the plan skill's vertical-slice rule): no — every child carries
  its own test acceptance criteria and names its test home in `**Key Files:**`, so each is
  a vertical slice (code + tests + docs) rather than a horizontal layer.
- Q: "Do the two lock-window children need sequencing?"
  Answer (agent): yes — the bounded-wait default (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF) changes the same
  `phase_finish` lock-acquisition path that SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4 shrinks; installing a
  positive bound before the suite leaves the lock would introduce long (bounded) waits
  around a still-locked full suite. Dependency edge added:
  SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF depends on SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4.
- Review note (no decision needed): `.githooks/pre-push` is flagged by
  `validate_key_files_format()` only because hook scripts carry no file extension; the
  path is correct and was deliberately left unchanged.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4** – Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (open)
- **SA-0MPVO6JNI006ESN0** – Triage dev-full-suite failures (run 26780355787) (completed)
- **SA-0MW6VXSF8004X1PK** – [test-failure] post-push full-suite verification: no valid full-suite cache entry — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, 0mvpzg3iq009ijmo, 0mw22semv00230o5, accept, acceptance (+333 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, absorbing, accept, acceptance, acquires (+329 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, 0mvnqurzm001tkjy, 0mvpzg3iq009ijmo, 0mw22semv00230o5, accept (+320 more)
